strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Turns M9.4 metadata-only selection handles into an executable selected-file context read while preserving index provenance.
Adds one controlled built-in tool path under tool.execute for exactly one selected index read, using the existing workspace read boundary.
Requires ReadWorkspace through the built-in tool registry and a secondary RuntimeAction::IndexCodebase check before current snapshot or file reads.
Records CodebaseIndexSelectionReadCompleted as summary-only evidence with ids, fingerprints, counts, byte counts, content hash status, and path fingerprints.
Lets unattended callers proceed from codebase.index.query selection handles to bounded file context without caller-side path scraping or external policy decisions.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances codebase_indexing directly, with supporting progress for controlled_workspace_tools, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: Brownie can now consume a bounded codebase.index.query selection handle through tool.execute(codebase.index.selection.read), validate query/snapshot/selection/hash provenance, and return one selected file's bounded UTF-8 content.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Plain workspace.read can read a caller-supplied safe path, but it cannot prove that the path came from a prior index query, validate the current snapshot and selected entry hash, or record replay-safe index-selection read evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless callers would still have to copy selected paths from M9.4 into plain workspace reads and own the policy glue outside the Rust runtime, leaving index-guided context materialization unaudited and stale-selection prone.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M9.2.1 fixed index-build integrity, M9.3 filtered ignored and sensitive files, and M9.4 returned metadata-only selection handles. M9.5 executes one validated selected-file read from those handles.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase deliberately uses the existing tool.execute method and registers one built-in tool id instead of adding a JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, preview, history, verdict, readiness, or inspection surface. The only new persistent record is the required summary-only ledger evidence for the successful selected read.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime now handles codebase.index.selection.read by checking ReadWorkspace and IndexCodebase permissions, validating bounded input and prior query evidence, matching the current snapshot entry, rejecting symlinks/directories/unsafe paths, reading one file through the controlled workspace boundary, verifying post-read SHA-256, and appending CodebaseIndexSelectionReadCompleted.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless caller can run build -> query -> selected read and receive bounded context plus stable replay evidence without scraping current.json or making its own path authorization decision.
answers.milestone_progress: M9 moves from snapshot build and metadata selection to actual runtime-owned context materialization, the next necessary step before prompt materialization, retrieval, or symbol/chunk work.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M9.5 updates the deterministic current phase manifest and archives the M9.5 value gate. Review must confirm this is an executable selected-index-read tool path under tool.execute, not a new wrapper or report surface.

exit_criteria: codebase.index.selection.read is registered as a built-in ReadWorkspace tool and is invoked through existing tool.execute
No new JSON-RPC method is added for selected index reads
The runtime performs a secondary RuntimeAction::IndexCodebase check before reading current index state, query ledger evidence, or file content

Selected-read input rejects unknown fields, malformed ids or fingerprints, unsafe paths, parent traversal, absolute paths, protected paths, unsupported file kinds, missing content hashes, and oversized selected-entry arrays
The runtime recomputes selection_fingerprint from supplied bounded entries and requires selection_id plus prior CodebaseIndexQueryCompleted evidence to match
The latest current snapshot identity and selected entry metadata must match the selection binding before file content is returned
The selected file is read through the controlled workspace read boundary and symlinks, directories, missing files, invalid UTF-8, and truncation fail safely
Post-read SHA-256 must match the selected entry content_sha256 before a successful result or success event is returned
Successful selected reads return bounded UTF-8 content and metadata in the explicit tool result

Successful selected reads append exactly one summary-only CodebaseIndexSelectionReadCompleted event without raw query text, raw selected paths, raw file content, snippets, diffs, stdout/stderr, environment values, commands, prompts, provider responses, absolute paths, or canonical paths

VSIX validators accept the M9.5 selected-read result shape and reject raw-query/raw-content leak fields, unsafe paths, stale event kinds, stale next_action, invalid file kinds, invalid fingerprints, truncation, and unbounded content
No report, digest, history, readiness wrapper, batch read, chunking, embeddings, Qdrant writes, LLM calls, shell/git/network/service execution, or workspace mutation is added

test_tokens: validates selected index read results with bounded explicit content
